question: Should AWS G6 ephemeral workers be allowed to execute stateful model jobs (jobs whose correctness depends on state kept on the worker between invocations)? Decide: accept (allow stateful), reject (stateless only), request_changes or request_more_evidence.

evidence.text: Every stop/start of the G6 changes its public IP; the control plane must resync the WireGuard endpoint (wg-sync). Verified across multiple starts on 2026-07-03/04 (endpoints 18.101.186.131, 15.216.147.179, 15.217.12.130).

A reaper stops the G6 after 300s without vLLM requests (Prometheus vllm:num_requests_running == 0 sustained); shutdown can happen at any moment between jobs and is logged with timestamps. The shutdown policy is part of the platform design, not an accident.
The G6's EBS volume (100GB: model weights, container images) persists across stop/start — disk state survives, but process/GPU memory state does not.

g6 capacity in eu-south-2a is scarce: starts fail with capacity errors and need retries (observed repeatedly; first start attempt failed on 3 of 4 session starts on 2026-07-03/04). A worker may not come back promptly after a stop.

The choreographer's agent/council registry is in-memory per pod: engine-side state also does not survive restarts. The platform's persistence model is: evidence persists (S3/Tempo/Loki/Prometheus), compute state does not.
